\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The uncertainty principle in the finite setting}
Uncertainty principles quantify the impossibility of a function and its Fourier transform being
simultaneously concentrated. On a finite abelian group $G$ of order $N$, concentration admits the
crudest and cleanest measure imaginable: the cardinality of the support. The resulting statement,
due to Donoho and Stark, is that for every nonzero $f:G\to\C$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ds}
  |\supp f|\cdot|\supp\dual f|\;\ge\;N.
\end{equation}
The inequality is elementary --- a two-line consequence of Plancherel and Cauchy--Schwarz --- but
its consequences are not. It is the combinatorial heart of compressive sensing: a signal supported
on $k$ points has at least $N/k$ nonzero Fourier coefficients, so a sparse signal cannot
masquerade as a sparse spectrum.

Equality is attained. For any subgroup $H\le G$, coset $a+H$, character $\chi$ and $c\ne0$, the
\emph{modulated coset indicator}
\[
  f(x)=\begin{cases} c\,\chi(x), & x-a\in H,\\ 0,& x-a\notin H,\end{cases}
\]
has $|\supp f|=|H|$ and $|\supp\dual f|=|H^{\perp}|$, and the duality $|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}|=N$ gives
equality.

\subsection{The result}
The converse --- that these are the \emph{only} extremals --- is the rigidity phenomenon we
establish (Theorem~\ref{thm:main}). The interest lies less in the statement than in the mechanism:
the proof isolates four separate rigidity phenomena, each an equality case of a standard
inequality, and shows how they compose. The last of them, the appearance of a canonical subgroup
out of pure phase data, carries all the arithmetic content and is the step that resists
generalisation.

The first three stages yield two attractive necessary conditions: $|f|$ constant on $\supp f$ and
$|\dual f|$ constant on $\supp\dual f$. It is natural to conjecture that these \emph{bi-flatness}
conditions are sufficient. We refute this in every nontrivial case (Section~\ref{sec:counter}):
the discrete chirp on a self-dual group is bi-flat in the strongest sense yet maximally
non-extremal.

\section{Setting and notation}

Throughout, $G$ is a finite abelian group written additively, $N:=|G|\ge1$.

\begin{definition}[Character]
A \emph{character} of $G$ is a map $\psi:G\to\C^{\times}$ with $\psi(x+y)=\psi(x)\psi(y)$. Since
$G$ is finite, each $\psi(x)$ is a root of unity; in particular $|\psi(x)|=1$ and
$\psi(-x)=\overline{\psi(x)}=\psi(x)^{-1}$.
\end{definition}

The characters form an abelian group $\dual G$ under pointwise multiplication, written additively:
$(\psi+\chi)(x)=\psi(x)\chi(x)$, with identity the trivial character $0:x\mapsto1$, and
$(\psi-\chi)(x)=\psi(x)\overline{\chi(x)}$.

\begin{fact}[Pontryagin duality]\label{fact:pont}
$|\dual G|=|G|$, and the double-dual embedding $\iota:G\to\dual{\dual G}$ sending $x$ to the
evaluation character $\psi\mapsto\psi(x)$ is a group isomorphism.
\end{fact}

\begin{fact}[Orthogonality]\label{fact:orth}
For $x\in G$, $\sum_{\psi\in\dual G}\psi(x)=N$ if $x=0$ and $0$ otherwise; dually
$\sum_{x\in G}\psi(x)=N$ if $\psi=0$ and $0$ otherwise. Equivalently
$\sum_{\psi}\psi(x)\overline{\psi(z)}=N\,[x=z]$.
\end{fact}

\begin{definition}[Annihilator]
For $H\le G$, $H^{\perp}:=\{\psi\in\dual G:\psi(h)=1\ \forall h\in H\}\le\dual G$.
\end{definition}

\begin{fact}[Subgroup duality]\label{fact:dual}
$|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}|=N$; indeed $H^{\perp}\cong\dual{(G/H)}$, of order $N/|H|$.
\end{fact}

Fact~\ref{fact:dual} is the arithmetic engine of the whole paper.

\begin{definition}[Fourier transform]
For $f:G\to\C$ put $\dual f(\psi):=\sum_{x\in G}\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)$, $\psi\in\dual G$.
\end{definition}

\begin{fact}[Inversion]\label{fact:inv}
$N f(x)=\sum_{\psi\in\dual G}\psi(x)\dual f(\psi)$ for all $x$; in particular the transform is
injective, and $\dual{\dual f}(\iota(x))=N f(-x)$.
\end{fact}

\begin{fact}[Plancherel]\label{fact:planch}
$\sum_{\psi\in\dual G}|\dual f(\psi)|^2=N\sum_{x\in G}|f(x)|^2$.
\end{fact}

\begin{definition}[Supports, norms, extremality]
$\supp f:=\{x:f(x)\ne0\}$, and analogously $\supp\dual f\subseteq\dual G$. We write
$\|f\|_1=\sum_x|f(x)|$ and $\|f\|_2^2=\sum_x|f(x)|^2$. The function $f$ is \emph{extremal} if
\[
  |\supp f|\cdot|\supp\dual f|=N.
\]
An extremal function is automatically nonzero, since for $f=0$ both supports are empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Modulated coset indicator]
$f$ \emph{is a modulated coset indicator} if there are $H\le G$, $c\ne0$, $\chi\in\dual G$ and
$a\in G$ with $f(x)=c\chi(x)$ whenever $x-a\in H$ and $f(x)=0$ whenever $x-a\notin H$. We write
$f=c\,\chi\,\one_{a+H}$.
\end{definition}

\section{The easy direction, made explicit}

\begin{theorem}[Transform of a modulated coset indicator]\label{thm:dftcoset}
Let $H\le G$, $c\in\C$, $\chi\in\dual G$, $a\in G$ and $f=c\,\chi\,\one_{a+H}$. Then for every
$\psi\in\dual G$,
\[
  \dual f(\psi)=c\,\overline{(\psi-\chi)(a)}\cdot
  \begin{cases}|H|,&\psi-\chi\in H^{\perp},\\ 0,&\psi-\chi\notin H^{\perp}.\end{cases}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The transform intertwines the three elementary operations: $\dual{cf}=c\dual f$;
$\dual{\chi f}(\psi)=\dual f(\psi-\chi)$; and $\dual{f(\cdot-a)}(\psi)=\overline{\psi(a)}\dual
f(\psi)$. It therefore suffices to transform $\one_H$, and orthogonality on $H$ gives
$\dual{\one_H}(\psi)=\sum_{h\in H}\overline{\psi(h)}=|H|\,[\psi\in H^{\perp}]$, since $\psi|_H$ is
a character of $H$, trivial exactly when $\psi\in H^{\perp}$ and otherwise summing to zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spectrum of an extremal]\label{cor:spectrum}
If $c\ne0$ then $\supp\dual f=\chi+H^{\perp}$. The extremal picture is self-dual in form: a
modulated coset indicator on $a+H$ has a transform which is a modulated coset indicator on
$\chi+H^{\perp}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Easy direction]\label{cor:easy}
Every modulated coset indicator with $c\ne0$ is extremal: $|\supp f|=|H|$,
$|\supp\dual f|=|H^{\perp}|$, and $|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}|=N$.
\end{corollary}

\section{Rigidity: the four-stage equality analysis}

Fix a nonzero $f$ and write $S=\supp f$, $A=\supp\dual f$. Since $f$ vanishes off $S$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sumsupp}
  \dual f(\psi)=\sum_{x\in S}\overline{\psi(x)}f(x),
\end{equation}
whence, by the triangle inequality and unimodularity of characters,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:l1bound}
  |\dual f(\psi)|\le\sum_{x\in S}|f(x)|=\|f\|_1\qquad\text{for all }\psi.
\end{equation}
Moreover $\|f\|_1>0$, and $\dual f\ne0$ by injectivity, so $S$ and $A$ are nonempty.

\subsection{Stage 1: the spectrum is flat}

\begin{theorem}[Flat spectrum]\label{thm:flatspec}
If $f$ is extremal then $|\dual f(\psi)|=\|f\|_1$ for every $\psi\in A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Restricting Plancherel to the spectrum (omitted terms vanish) gives
$\sum_{\psi\in A}|\dual f(\psi)|^2=N\|f\|_2^2$, so by \eqref{eq:l1bound}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:step1}
  N\|f\|_2^2\le|A|\cdot\|f\|_1^2 .
\end{equation}
Cauchy--Schwarz on the support gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:step2}
  \|f\|_1^2\le|S|\cdot\|f\|_2^2 .
\end{equation}
Chaining yields $N\|f\|_2^2\le|A||S|\|f\|_2^2$, i.e.\ \eqref{eq:ds}. Under extremality
$|S||A|=N$, so both \eqref{eq:step1} and \eqref{eq:step2} are equalities. Equality in
\eqref{eq:step1} forces each term $|\dual f(\psi)|^2$, $\psi\in A$, to attain its common upper
bound $\|f\|_1^2$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Stage 2: phase alignment}

\begin{lemma}[Equality in the triangle inequality]\label{lem:triangle}
Let $z:I\to\C$ be a finite family with $\bigl|\sum_j z_j\bigr|=\sum_j|z_j|$, and set
$T=\sum_j z_j$. Then $|T|\,z_i=|z_i|\,T$ for every $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
If $T=0$ then all $z_j=0$. Otherwise set $w=\overline T/|T|$, unimodular with $wT=|T|$. For each
$j$, $\Rea(wz_j)\le|wz_j|=|z_j|$, while $\sum_j\Rea(wz_j)=\Rea(wT)=|T|=\sum_j|z_j|$. A sum of
termwise inequalities that is an equality is an equality termwise, so $\Rea(wz_i)=|wz_i|$; a
complex number whose real part equals its modulus is that nonnegative real, so $wz_i=|z_i|$.
Multiplying by $T$ and using $wT=|T|$ gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Phase alignment]\label{thm:align}
Let $f$ be extremal, $\psi\in A$, $x\in S$. Then
\[
  \|f\|_1\cdot\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)=|f(x)|\cdot\dual f(\psi).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:triangle} to $z_x=\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)$, $x\in S$, whose sum is
$\dual f(\psi)$ by \eqref{eq:sumsupp} and whose moduli are $|f(x)|$; the hypothesis is exactly
Theorem~\ref{thm:flatspec}.
\end{proof}

At each spectral frequency, the demodulated samples $\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)$, $x\in S$, are all
nonnegative multiples of the single number $\dual f(\psi)$.

\subsection{Stage 3: the modulus is flat}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp value distribution]\label{thm:flatmod}
Let $f$ be extremal. Then $|f(x)|\cdot N=\|f\|_1\cdot|A|$ for every $x\in S$; equivalently
$|f(x)|=\|f\|_1/|S|$. In particular $|f|$ is constant on $\supp f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Fix $x\in S$. Inversion restricted to the spectrum gives
$Nf(x)=\sum_{\psi\in A}\psi(x)\dual f(\psi)$. Multiplying by $|f(x)|$ and using
Theorem~\ref{thm:align} termwise,
\[
  |f(x)|\,\psi(x)\dual f(\psi)=\psi(x)\bigl(\|f\|_1\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)\bigr)=\|f\|_1 f(x),
\]
independently of $\psi$. Hence $|f(x)|\,Nf(x)=|A|\,\|f\|_1 f(x)$; cancel $f(x)\ne0$ to obtain
$|f(x)|N=\|f\|_1|A|$. The right side is independent of $x$, and substituting $N=|S||A|$ and
cancelling $|A|>0$ gives $|f(x)|\,|S|=\|f\|_1$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Stage 4: the phase subgroup and the counting argument}

\begin{corollary}[Total demodulated coherence]\label{cor:coherence}
Let $f$ be extremal, $\psi\in A$, $x,y\in S$. Then
$\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)=\overline{\psi(y)}f(y)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:align} both sides equal $|f(x)|\dual f(\psi)/\|f\|_1$, using
$|f(x)|=|f(y)|$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:flatmod}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Phase subgroup]\label{def:phase}
For $f:G\to\C$ and $\psi_0\in\dual G$ put
\[
  H_{f,\psi_0}:=\{z\in G:\psi(z)=\psi_0(z)\ \text{for all }\psi\in\supp\dual f\}
  \;=\;\bigcap_{\psi\in\supp\dual f}\ker(\psi-\psi_0).
\]
It is a subgroup: it contains $0$ and each defining condition is multiplicative in $z$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Differences lie in the phase subgroup]\label{lem:diff}
Let $f$ be extremal, $\psi_0\in A$, $x,y\in S$. Then $x-y\in H:=H_{f,\psi_0}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For $\psi\in A$, Corollary~\ref{cor:coherence} applied to $\psi$ and to $\psi_0$ gives
$\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)=\overline{\psi(y)}f(y)$ and
$\overline{\psi_0(x)}f(x)=\overline{\psi_0(y)}f(y)$. All quantities are nonzero; dividing the
first by the second yields $\overline{(\psi-\psi_0)(x)}=\overline{(\psi-\psi_0)(y)}$, i.e.\
$(\psi-\psi_0)(x-y)=1$, i.e.\ $\psi(x-y)=\psi_0(x-y)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:annih}
With the same hypotheses, $\psi-\psi_0\in H^{\perp}$ for every $\psi\in A$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Support is exactly a coset]\label{thm:coset}
Let $f$ be extremal, $\psi_0\in A$, $a\in S$, $H=H_{f,\psi_0}$. Then $x\in\supp f\iff x-a\in H$.
Consequently $\supp f=a+H$ and $\supp\dual f=\psi_0+H^{\perp}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The forward implication is Lemma~\ref{lem:diff} with $y=a$. Conversely, $y\mapsto y-a$ is an
injection $S\hookrightarrow H$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:diff}, so $|S|\le|H|$; and
$\psi\mapsto\psi-\psi_0$ is an injection $A\hookrightarrow H^{\perp}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:annih}, so
$|A|\le|H^{\perp}|$. Multiplying and using extremality with Fact~\ref{fact:dual},
\[
  N=|S|\cdot|A|\le|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}|=N,
\]
so both inequalities are equalities; injections between finite sets of equal cardinality are
bijections, whence $S-a=H$ and $A-\psi_0=H^{\perp}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Main Theorem: Rigidity]\label{thm:main}
$f$ is extremal if and only if $f$ is a modulated coset indicator with $c\ne0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Leftarrow$) Corollary~\ref{cor:easy}. ($\Rightarrow$) Pick $a\in S$, $\psi_0\in A$, set
$H=H_{f,\psi_0}$ and $c=\overline{\psi_0(a)}f(a)\ne0$. If $x-a\in H$ then $x\in S$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:coset}, and Corollary~\ref{cor:coherence} gives
$\overline{\psi_0(x)}f(x)=c$, so $f(x)=c\,\psi_0(x)$. If $x-a\notin H$ then $x\notin S$, i.e.\
$f(x)=0$.
\end{proof}

\section{Structural consequences}

Throughout, $f$ is extremal, $S=\supp f$, $A=\supp\dual f$.

\begin{theorem}[Coset closure]\label{thm:closure}
If $x,y,z\in S$ then $x-y+z\in S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix $\psi_0\in A$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:diff}, $(x-y+z)-z=x-y\in H_{f,\psi_0}$; apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:coset} with base point $z\in S$.
\end{proof}

A nonempty subset of an abelian group closed under $(x,y,z)\mapsto x-y+z$ is exactly a coset of a
subgroup, so this is cosetness stated with no auxiliary data.

\begin{lemma}[Support of the double transform]\label{lem:double}
$\supp\dual{\dual f}=\{\iota(-x):x\in\supp f\}$, where $\iota$ is the double-dual embedding.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Every element of $\dual{\dual G}$ is $\iota(x)$ for a unique $x$ (Fact~\ref{fact:pont}), and
$\dual{\dual f}(\iota(x))=Nf(-x)$ with $N\ne0$ (Fact~\ref{fact:inv}).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Extremality is self-dual]\label{thm:selfdual}
If $f$ is extremal on $G$ then $\dual f$ is extremal on $\dual G$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:double} and injectivity of $x\mapsto\iota(-x)$,
$|\supp\dual{\dual f}|=|S|$, so $|\supp\dual f|\cdot|\supp\dual{\dual f}|=|A||S|=N=|\dual G|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Phase subgroup $=$ period group]\label{thm:period}
Let $f$ be extremal and $\psi_0\in A$. For $z\in G$,
\[
  z\in H_{f,\psi_0}\iff\bigl(x\in\supp f\Rightarrow x+z\in\supp f\bigr).
\]
In particular $H_{f,\psi_0}=\{z:S+z=S\}$ is independent of the choice of $\psi_0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Fix $a\in S$. If $z\in H$ and $x\in S$ then $(x+z)-a=(x-a)+z\in H$, so $x+z\in S$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:coset}. Conversely, if $S+z\subseteq S$ then $a+z\in S$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:diff}
gives $z=(a+z)-a\in H$. The right-hand condition does not mention $\psi_0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Support of a modulated coset indicator]\label{thm:suppcoset}
If $f=c\chi\one_{a+H}$ with $c\ne0$, then $x\in\supp f\iff x-a\in H$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The subgroup is unique]\label{thm:unique}
If $c_1\chi_1\one_{a_1+H_1}=c_2\chi_2\one_{a_2+H_2}$ as functions with $c_1,c_2\ne0$, then
$H_1=H_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:suppcoset}, $x-a_1\in H_1\iff x-a_2\in H_2$ for all $x$. Taking $x=a_1$ gives
$a_1-a_2\in H_2$. For arbitrary $z$, substituting $x=z+a_1$ gives
$z\in H_1\iff z+(a_1-a_2)\in H_2\iff z\in H_2$, since $H_2$ is a subgroup containing $a_1-a_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Extremals with fixed support form one orbit]\label{thm:orbit}
If $f$ and $g$ are extremal with $\supp f=\supp g$, then there are $c\ne0$ and $\chi\in\dual G$
with $f(x)=c\,\chi(x)\,g(x)$ for all $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Write $f=c_1\chi_1\one_{a_1+H_1}$ and $g=c_2\chi_2\one_{a_2+H_2}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. On
the common support $f=c_1\chi_1$ and $g=c_2\chi_2$, so $f=(c_1/c_2)(\chi_1-\chi_2)g$ there; off it
both sides vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Global description]\label{cor:global}
The extremal set is the disjoint union, over all cosets $a+H$ of all subgroups $H\le G$, of a
single orbit of $\C^{\times}\times\dual G$ acting by scaling and modulation. Two pairs
$(c,\chi)$, $(c',\chi')$ give the same function precisely when $\chi-\chi'\in H^{\perp}$ and
$c'\chi'(a)=c\chi(a)$.
\end{corollary}

\section{Arithmetic consequences}

\begin{theorem}[Divisibility obstruction]\label{thm:dvd}
If $f$ is extremal then $|\supp f|$ divides $N$, and $|\supp\dual f|=N/|\supp f|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharpness]\label{thm:sharp}
Conversely, for every $H\le G$ and $a\in G$ there is an extremal $g$ with $\supp g=a+H$; take
$g=\one_{a+H}$.
\end{theorem}

Thus the possible extremal support sizes are exactly the orders of subgroups of $G$: for
$G=\Z/N$, the divisors of $N$; for $G=(\Z/p)^n$, the powers $p^k$, $0\le k\le n$.

\begin{theorem}[Prime dichotomy]\label{thm:prime}
Suppose $N=|G|$ is prime and $f$ is extremal. Then either
\begin{enumerate}
  \item there are $a\in G$, $c\ne0$ with $f=c\,\delta_a$; or
  \item there are $c\ne0$, $\chi\in\dual G$ with $f(x)=c\,\chi(x)$ for all $x$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$|S|$ divides the prime $N$, hence equals $1$ or $N$. If $|S|=1$, say $S=\{a\}$, then $f=f(a)
\delta_a$. If $|S|=N$ then $S=G$, and the representation $f=c\chi\one_{a+H}$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} can exclude no point, so $f=c\chi$ everywhere.
\end{proof}

In prime order there is no intermediate extremal: the extremal set consists of $N$ lines of Dirac
deltas and $N$ lines of characters, $2N$ complex lines in $\C^N$.

\begin{theorem}[Uncertainty gap]\label{thm:gap}
Let $f\ne0$, suppose $|\supp f|$ divides $N$, and suppose $f$ is \emph{not} a modulated coset
indicator. Then
\[
  |\supp f|\cdot|\supp\dual f|\;\ge\;N+|\supp f| .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Write $N=|S|q$. By \eqref{eq:ds}, $|S||A|\ge N$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:main} rules out equality, so
$|S||A|>|S|q$, whence $|A|\ge q+1$ by integrality and
$|S||A|\ge|S|q+|S|=N+|S|$.
\end{proof}

Within the divisibility-constrained class the uncertainty product lies in $|S|\Z$, so it cannot
approach $N$ from above without reaching it: extremality is an isolated point of the value
spectrum. The divisibility hypothesis is necessary; without it the excess can be smaller than
$|S|$.

\begin{theorem}[Extremal sets are cosets]\label{thm:comb}
Let $S\subseteq G$ be nonempty. Then $|S|\cdot|\supp\dual{\one_S}|=N$ if and only if $S=a+H$ for
some $H\le G$ and $a\in G$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Leftarrow$) Corollary~\ref{cor:easy}. ($\Rightarrow$) $\supp\one_S=S$; apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:coset} with any $a\in S$ and any $\psi_0$ in the spectrum.
\end{proof}

Equivalently: cosets are exactly the sets whose Fourier sparsity is as small as the uncertainty
principle permits.

\section{Bi-flatness does not imply extremality}\label{sec:counter}

The rigidity proof yields two necessary conditions:
\begin{itemize}
  \item[(F1)] $|f|$ is constant on $\supp f$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:flatmod});
  \item[(F2)] $|\dual f|$ is constant on $\supp\dual f$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:flatspec}).
\end{itemize}
Call $f$ \emph{bi-flat} if both hold. We show that bi-flatness does not characterise extremality,
and fails maximally.

Let $K$ be a finite abelian group with $|K|>1$ and put $G:=K\times\dual K$, so $|G|=|K|^2$ and $G$
is isomorphic to its own dual. Define the \emph{evaluation pairing}
\[
  f:G\to\C,\qquad f(x,\psi):=\psi(x).
\]
For $K=\Z/n$, identifying $\dual K$ with $\Z/n$, this is the discrete \emph{chirp}
$f(x,y)=e^{2\pi i xy/n}$, the finite analogue of $e^{ix\xi}$.

\begin{proposition}[Flatness in space]\label{prop:flat1}
$|f(p)|=1$ for all $p\in G$; in particular $\supp f=G$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Flatness in frequency]\label{thm:flat2}
For every $\chi\in\dual G$, $|\dual f(\chi)|=|K|=\sqrt{|G|}$; in particular
$\supp\dual f=\dual G$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Restrict $\chi$ to the second factor: $\chi_2:=\chi(0,\cdot)\in\dual{\dual K}$. By
Fact~\ref{fact:pont} there is a unique $z\in K$ with $\chi_2(\psi)=\psi(z)$ for all $\psi$. Since
$\chi$ is a character of a product, $\chi(x,\psi)=\chi(x,0)\chi(0,\psi)=\chi(x,0)\psi(z)$. Hence
\[
  \dual f(\chi)=\sum_{x\in K}\overline{\chi(x,0)}\sum_{\psi\in\dual K}\psi(x)\overline{\psi(z)}
  =|K|\cdot\overline{\chi(z,0)}
\]
by orthogonality (Fact~\ref{fact:orth}), a unimodular number times $|K|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Maximal non-extremality]\label{thm:maxnon}
If $|K|>1$ then $|\supp f|\cdot|\supp\dual f|=|G|\cdot|\dual G|=|G|^2>|G|$, so $f$ is not
extremal. Indeed $|G|^2$ is the largest value the uncertainty product can take.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Bi-flatness is insufficient]\label{cor:biflat}
For every finite abelian $K$ with $|K|>1$ there is $f$ on $G=K\times\dual K$ with $|f|\equiv1$ on
$G$ and $|\dual f|\equiv\sqrt{|G|}$ on $\dual G$ --- so (F1) and (F2) hold in the strongest
possible form, with both supports full --- yet $f$ is not extremal. The smallest instance is
$K=\Z/2$, where $|G|=4$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}
The failure is instructive. Stages 1 and 3 produce (F1) and (F2), which are \emph{magnitude}
statements. Stage 2 together with Corollary~\ref{cor:coherence} produces something structurally
different: constancy of $x\mapsto\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)$ on $\supp f$ \emph{simultaneously for all
$\psi$ in the spectrum}. That is a coupling between different spectral frequencies, and it is what
makes Definition~\ref{def:phase} meaningful, the phase subgroup being an intersection over the
whole spectrum. The chirp maximally violates the coupling: its spectrum is everything, so the
intersection is trivial, and for each $\chi$ the demodulated function is genuinely non-constant.
Every frequency sees a perfectly balanced signal; no two frequencies agree about the phase
pattern; the energy stays spread. In engineering terms, bi-flat signals are exactly what radar and
spread-spectrum design want --- constant envelope in time, constant magnitude in frequency --- and
the theorem says this is the antipode of concentration.
\end{remark}

\section{Applications and context}

\textbf{Compressive sensing.} If distinct $k$-sparse signals agree on a frequency set $\Omega$,
their difference is $2k$-sparse with spectrum inside $\dual G\setminus\Omega$, so \eqref{eq:ds}
forces $|\Omega|\le N-N/(2k)$. Rigidity says which configurations are genuinely ambiguous: exactly
the picket fences, i.e.\ cosets. In prime order Theorem~\ref{thm:prime} leaves only deltas and
characters, which is why prime-length transforms admit uniform guarantees that composite lengths
do not.

\textbf{Hidden subgroup structure.} Definition~\ref{def:phase} is a spectral extraction of a
hidden subgroup: from the spectrum $A$ one forms $\bigcap_{\psi\in A}\ker(\psi-\psi_0)$ and
recovers $H$ exactly. Theorem~\ref{thm:period} states its correctness intrinsically.

\textbf{Coding theory.} Theorem~\ref{thm:comb} identifies cosets as the unique subsets of minimal
Fourier sparsity; since cosets are exactly translated linear subspaces, this characterises linear
codes among all codes of a given size by a spectral extremality property.

\textbf{Additive combinatorics.} ``Equality in a Fourier inequality forces exact algebraic
structure'' is a pervasive pattern; Theorem~\ref{thm:gap} sharpens it here to a genuine gap, so
that in the divisibility-constrained regime the transition from structured to unstructured is
discontinuous.

\textbf{Time--frequency analysis.} Theorem~\ref{thm:dftcoset} and Corollary~\ref{cor:spectrum}
record that the extremal family is closed under the transform with $H\mapsto H^{\perp}$
implementing the duality --- the finite shadow of transform-invariance of Gaussians, with the
coset lattice playing the role of the covariance.

\section{Open problems and future directions}

\begin{conjecture}[Stability]\label{conj:stab}
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every finite abelian $G$ and every $f\ne0$ with
$|\supp f|\cdot|\supp\dual f|\le(1+\varepsilon)|G|$ and $\varepsilon\le1/C$, there exist $H\le G$,
$\chi\in\dual G$, $a\in G$, $c\in\C$ with
$\|f-c\,\chi\,\one_{a+H}\|_2\le C\sqrt{\varepsilon}\,\|f\|_2$.
\end{conjecture}

The proof above is already quantitative in Stages 1--3: the inequalities \eqref{eq:step1} and
\eqref{eq:step2} are each within a factor $1+\varepsilon$ of equality, and the equality analyses
--- flatness of $|\dual f|$ on the spectrum and alignment of demodulated phases --- degrade
continuously. The genuinely discrete ingredient is the counting step of Theorem~\ref{thm:coset}:
two injections whose images have sizes multiplying to $N$. A stability theory needs an approximate
substitute, quantitatively compatible with $|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}|=N$. Theorem~\ref{thm:gap} shows
the discrete side of this picture is rigid, so the remaining content is analytic.

\begin{conjecture}[Exponent independence]\label{conj:l4}
If $f\ne0$ satisfies $\|\dual f\|_4^4\cdot|\supp f|=|G|\cdot\|f\|_2^4$ --- equality in the
$\ell^4$ form of the uncertainty principle obtained from Plancherel and H\"older --- then $\supp f$
is a coset and $f$ is a modulated coset indicator.
\end{conjecture}

Both inequalities are driven by the same two mechanisms (a H\"older step whose equality case forces
flatness, a triangle step whose equality case forces alignment), so the extremal family should be
independent of the exponent --- a $p$-independence phenomenon reminiscent of the equality cases of
Hausdorff--Young. Since $\|\dual f\|_4^4$ is the additive energy of $f$ up to normalisation, a
positive answer would identify cosets as the universal extremal family for finite Fourier
analysis.

\medskip

\noindent\textbf{Non-abelian analogues.} For a finite group the analogue of \eqref{eq:ds} involves
the Fourier support in the space of irreducible representations, weighted by dimension. Stages
1--3 survive for one-dimensional representations, but Definition~\ref{def:phase} uses commutativity
of character values. The Heisenberg group over $\Z/p$ --- where the chirp of
Section~\ref{sec:counter} is the natural object --- would be a decisive test case.

\medskip

\noindent\textbf{A quantitative coherence defect.} Define
$D(f)=\max_{\psi\in\supp\dual f}\max_{x,y\in\supp f}\bigl|\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)
-\overline{\psi(y)}f(y)\bigr|$. Rigidity says $D(f)=0$ for extremals; the chirp maximises $D$. Is
there a two-sided estimate relating $D(f)$ to the uncertainty excess
$|\supp f||\supp\dual f|/|G|-1$ for bi-flat $f$? Such an estimate would fuse the two halves of
this paper and supply the missing ingredient for Conjecture~\ref{conj:stab}.

\section{Conclusion}

Equality in the Donoho--Stark uncertainty principle is an extremely rigid condition: it determines
the support (a coset), the modulus (constant, equal to $\|f\|_1/|\supp f|$) and the phase (a
character), leaving only a scalar and a modulation free. The classification is self-dual, the
subgroup involved is canonical (the period group of the support), the extremal supports are
exactly the cosets, and --- within the class of functions whose support size divides $|G|$ ---
failure of extremality costs at least a full step of $|\supp f|$.

What makes the theorem work is not the flatness of $|f|$ or $|\dual f|$ but the coherence of the
demodulated signal across the whole spectrum at once. The discrete chirp on a self-dual group
demonstrates this decisively: bi-flat in the strongest possible sense, and as far from extremal as
any function can be. In finite Fourier analysis, magnitudes constrain; phases determine.

Rigidity of the Donoho-Stark uncertainty principle on finite abelian groups
===========================================================================

Numerical demonstrations, in pure Python (standard library only).

Setting
-------
A finite abelian group is presented as a tuple of moduli, e.g. ``(12,)`` for
Z/12 and ``(3, 3)`` for Z/3 x Z/3.  Its elements are tuples of residues.  The
dual group is identified with the group itself via the pairing

    chi_k(x) = exp(2*pi*i * sum_j k_j x_j / n_j),

and the (unnormalised) Fourier transform is

    fhat(k) = sum_x conj(chi_k(x)) f(x).

With N = |G|, the Donoho-Stark uncertainty principle states

    |supp f| * |supp fhat| >= N          for every f != 0,

and the rigidity theorem proved in the accompanying paper says that equality
holds exactly for the modulated coset indicators

    f = c * chi * 1_{a+H},   H <= G a subgroup, a in G, chi a character, c != 0.

The demonstrations below verify, numerically:

  1. modulated coset indicators are extremal, with the predicted spectrum
     chi + H^perp and the predicted flat modulus ||f||_1 / |supp f|;
  2. extremality is self-dual (the transform of an extremal is extremal);
  3. an indicator function is extremal iff its set is a coset (exhaustive
     search over all nonempty subsets of a small group);
  4. the arithmetic gap: if |supp f| divides N and f is not extremal, then
     the uncertainty product exceeds N by at least |supp f|;
  5. the prime-order dichotomy: extremals in prime order are scaled Dirac
     deltas or scaled characters;
  6. the bi-flat counterexample: on the self-dual group K x K^ the evaluation
     pairing (the discrete chirp) has |f| == 1 everywhere and |fhat| == sqrt(N)
     everywhere, yet its uncertainty product is N^2, the maximum possible;
  7. recovery of the phase subgroup from the spectrum, and the fact that it
     equals the group of periods of the support.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import itertools
import math
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Elt = Tuple[int, ...]
Group = Tuple[int, ...]
Func = Dict[Elt, complex]

TOL: float = 1e-9


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic group and Fourier machinery
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def elements(group: Group) -> List[Elt]:
    """All elements of the group Z/n_1 x ... x Z/n_k, in lexicographic order."""
    return [tuple(t) for t in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in group))]


def order(group: Group) -> int:
    """The order N = |G| of the group."""
    return math.prod(group)


def add(group: Group, x: Elt, y: Elt) -> Elt:
    """Group addition, componentwise modulo the respective moduli."""
    return tuple((a + b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def sub(group: Group, x: Elt, y: Elt) -> Elt:
    """Group subtraction, componentwise modulo the respective moduli."""
    return tuple((a - b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def pairing(group: Group, k: Elt, x: Elt) -> complex:
    """The character value chi_k(x) = exp(2*pi*i * sum_j k_j x_j / n_j)."""
    theta = 2.0 * math.pi * sum(kj * xj / n for kj, xj, n in zip(k, x, group))
    return cmath.exp(1j * theta)


def dft(group: Group, f: Func) -> Func:
    """Unnormalised Fourier transform: fhat(k) = sum_x conj(chi_k(x)) f(x)."""
    els = elements(group)
    return {
        k: sum(pairing(group, k, x).conjugate() * f[x] for x in els) for k in els
    }


def support(group: Group, f: Func) -> List[Elt]:
    """The set of points where f is nonzero (numerically, above TOL)."""
    return [x for x in elements(group) if abs(f[x]) > TOL]


def uncertainty_product(group: Group, f: Func) -> int:
    """|supp f| * |supp fhat|."""
    return len(support(group, f)) * len(support(group, dft(group, f)))


def is_extremal(group: Group, f: Func) -> bool:
    """True iff |supp f| * |supp fhat| == |G| (with f != 0)."""
    return len(support(group, f)) > 0 and uncertainty_product(group, f) == order(group)


def l1_norm(group: Group, f: Func) -> float:
    """The l^1 norm sum_x |f(x)|."""
    return sum(abs(f[x]) for x in elements(group))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subgroups, cosets, annihilators
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def subgroup_generated(group: Group, gens: Sequence[Elt]) -> List[Elt]:
    """The subgroup of G generated by the given elements (closure under +)."""
    zero: Elt = tuple(0 for _ in group)
    seen = {zero}
    frontier = [zero]
    while frontier:
        current = frontier.pop()
        for g in gens:
            nxt = add(group, current, g)
            if nxt not in seen:
                seen.add(nxt)
                frontier.append(nxt)
    return sorted(seen)


def all_subgroups(group: Group) -> List[Tuple[Elt, ...]]:
    """All subgroups of G, found by closing every subset of generators."""
    els = elements(group)
    found = set()
    # every subgroup of a finite abelian group of small rank is generated by
    # at most rank(G) elements; two generators suffice for the groups used here
    for r in range(0, 3):
        for gens in itertools.combinations(els, r):
            found.add(tuple(subgroup_generated(group, gens)))
    return sorted(found, key=lambda h: (len(h), h))


def annihilator(group: Group, H: Sequence[Elt]) -> List[Elt]:
    """H^perp = { k : chi_k(h) = 1 for all h in H }."""
    return [
        k
        for k in elements(group)
        if all(abs(pairing(group, k, h) - 1.0) < TOL for h in H)
    ]


def is_coset(group: Group, S: Sequence[Elt]) -> bool:
    """True iff the nonempty set S is a coset a + H of some subgroup H."""
    if not S:
        return False
    a = S[0]
    shifted = sorted(sub(group, s, a) for s in S)
    # a shifted copy is a subgroup iff it is closed under addition
    shifted_set = set(shifted)
    return all(add(group, u, v) in shifted_set for u in shifted for v in shifted)


def coset_modulation(
    group: Group, H: Sequence[Elt], a: Elt, chi: Elt, c: complex
) -> Func:
    """The modulated coset indicator f = c * chi_chi * 1_{a+H}."""
    Hset = set(H)
    return {
        x: (c * pairing(group, chi, x) if sub(group, x, a) in Hset else 0j)
        for x in elements(group)
    }


def indicator(group: Group, S: Iterable[Elt]) -> Func:
    """The 0/1 indicator function of a subset S of G."""
    Sset = set(S)
    return {x: (1.0 + 0j if x in Sset else 0j) for x in elements(group)}


def phase_subgroup(group: Group, f: Func) -> List[Elt]:
    """
    { z : chi_k(z) = chi_k0(z) for every k in supp fhat },
    where k0 is the first spectral frequency.  For an extremal f this is the
    period group of supp f.
    """
    spectrum = support(group, dft(group, f))
    k0 = spectrum[0]
    return [
        z
        for z in elements(group)
        if all(
            abs(pairing(group, k, z) - pairing(group, k0, z)) < TOL for k in spectrum
        )
    ]


def period_group(group: Group, S: Sequence[Elt]) -> List[Elt]:
    """{ z : S + z = S }, the group of periods of the set S."""
    Sset = set(S)
    return [z for z in elements(group) if {add(group, s, z) for s in Sset} == Sset]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def demo_coset_modulations_are_extremal() -> None:
    """1. Modulated coset indicators saturate the uncertainty principle."""
    print("=" * 76)
    print("1. Modulated coset indicators are extremal")
    print("=" * 76)
    group: Group = (12,)
    N = order(group)
    print(f"G = Z/12,  N = {N}\n")
    header = f"{'|H|':>4} {'a':>6} {'chi':>4} {'|supp f|':>9} {'|supp fhat|':>12} {'product':>8} {'|f| on supp':>12}"
    print(header)
    print("-" * len(header))
    for H in all_subgroups(group):
        a: Elt = (5,)
        chi: Elt = (3,)
        c = 2.0 * cmath.exp(0.7j)
        f = coset_modulation(group, H, a, chi, c)
        S = support(group, f)
        A = support(group, dft(group, f))
        modulus = {round(abs(f[x]), 9) for x in S}
        predicted = l1_norm(group, f) / len(S)
        assert len(S) * len(A) == N
        assert len(modulus) == 1 and abs(modulus.pop() - predicted) < 1e-8
        assert sorted(A) == sorted(
            add(group, chi, k) for k in annihilator(group, H)
        ), "spectrum must be chi + H^perp"
        print(
            f"{len(H):>4} {str(a):>6} {str(chi):>4} {len(S):>9} {len(A):>12} "
            f"{len(S) * len(A):>8} {predicted:>12.6f}"
        )
    print("\nEvery product equals N = 12; the spectrum is exactly chi + H^perp;")
    print("and |f| is constant on the support with value ||f||_1 / |supp f|.\n")


def demo_self_duality() -> None:
    """2. The Fourier transform of an extremal is extremal."""
    print("=" * 76)
    print("2. Extremality is self-dual")
    print("=" * 76)
    group: Group = (3, 3)
    N = order(group)
    H = subgroup_generated(group, [(1, 0)])
    f = coset_modulation(group, H, (0, 2), (1, 1), 1.5 - 0.5j)
    fhat = dft(group, f)
    p1 = uncertainty_product(group, f)
    p2 = uncertainty_product(group, fhat)
    print(f"G = Z/3 x Z/3,  N = {N},  H = <(1,0)> of order {len(H)}")
    print(f"  uncertainty product of f     : {p1}")
    print(f"  uncertainty product of fhat  : {p2}")
    assert p1 == N and p2 == N
    print("Both equal N: the extremal family is closed under the transform.\n")


def demo_indicator_extremal_iff_coset() -> None:
    """3. Exhaustive check: 1_S is extremal iff S is a coset."""
    print("=" * 76)
    print("3. An indicator function is extremal exactly when its set is a coset")
    print("=" * 76)
    group: Group = (6,)
    els = elements(group)
    N = order(group)
    extremal_sets: List[Tuple[Elt, ...]] = []
    mismatches = 0
    for r in range(1, N + 1):
        for S in itertools.combinations(els, r):
            ext = is_extremal(group, indicator(group, S))
            cos = is_coset(group, S)
            if ext != cos:
                mismatches += 1
            if ext:
                extremal_sets.append(S)
    print(f"G = Z/6: searched all {2 ** N - 1} nonempty subsets.")
    print(f"  extremal subsets : {len(extremal_sets)}")
    print(f"  mismatches with 'is a coset' : {mismatches}")
    for S in extremal_sets:
        print(f"    {sorted(x[0] for x in S)}")
    assert mismatches == 0
    print("The extremal sets are precisely the 12 cosets of the 4 subgroups.\n")


def demo_gap_theorem() -> None:
    """4. The arithmetic gap above the extremal locus."""
    print("=" * 76)
    print("4. Gap theorem: no near-extremal regime when |supp f| divides N")
    print("=" * 76)
    group: Group = (8,)
    els = elements(group)
    N = order(group)
    worst = None
    checked = 0
    for r in (1, 2, 4, 8):  # the divisors of 8
        for S in itertools.combinations(els, r):
            f = indicator(group, S)
            prod = uncertainty_product(group, f)
            if prod == N:
                continue
            checked += 1
            assert prod >= N + r, (S, prod)
            excess = prod - N
            if worst is None or excess < worst[1]:
                worst = (S, excess, r)
    print(f"G = Z/8, N = {N}.  Checked {checked} non-extremal 0/1 signals whose")
    print("support size divides N.  In every case the uncertainty product exceeded")
    print("N by at least |supp f|.")
    if worst is not None:
        S, excess, r = worst
        print(
            f"  smallest excess observed: {excess} (support size {r}, "
            f"set {sorted(x[0] for x in S)})"
        )
    print()


def demo_prime_dichotomy() -> None:
    """5. In prime order the only extremals are deltas and characters."""
    print("=" * 76)
    print("5. Prime-order dichotomy")
    print("=" * 76)
    group: Group = (7,)
    els = elements(group)
    N = order(group)
    sizes = set()
    for r in range(1, N + 1):
        for S in itertools.combinations(els, r):
            if is_extremal(group, indicator(group, S)):
                sizes.add(len(S))
    print(f"G = Z/7, N = {N} prime.")

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import itertools
import math
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Elt = Tuple[int, ...]
Group = Tuple[int, ...]
Func = Dict[Elt, complex]

TOL: float = 1e-9


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic group and Fourier machinery
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def elements(group: Group) -> List[Elt]:
    """All elements of the group Z/n_1 x ... x Z/n_k, in lexicographic order."""
    return [tuple(t) for t in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in group))]


def order(group: Group) -> int:
    """The order N = |G| of the group."""
    return math.prod(group)


def add(group: Group, x: Elt, y: Elt) -> Elt:
    """Group addition, componentwise modulo the respective moduli."""
    return tuple((a + b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def sub(group: Group, x: Elt, y: Elt) -> Elt:
    """Group subtraction, componentwise modulo the respective moduli."""
    return tuple((a - b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def pairing(group: Group, k: Elt, x: Elt) -> complex:
    """The character value chi_k(x) = exp(2*pi*i * sum_j k_j x_j / n_j)."""
    theta = 2.0 * math.pi * sum(kj * xj / n for kj, xj, n in zip(k, x, group))
    return cmath.exp(1j * theta)


def dft(group: Group, f: Func) -> Func:
    """Unnormalised Fourier transform: fhat(k) = sum_x conj(chi_k(x)) f(x)."""
    els = elements(group)
    return {
        k: sum(pairing(group, k, x).conjugate() * f[x] for x in els) for k in els
    }


def support(group: Group, f: Func) -> List[Elt]:
    """The set of points where f is nonzero (numerically, above TOL)."""
    return [x for x in elements(group) if abs(f[x]) > TOL]


def uncertainty_product(group: Group, f: Func) -> int:
    """|supp f| * |supp fhat|."""
    return len(support(group, f)) * len(support(group, dft(group, f)))


def is_extremal(group: Group, f: Func) -> bool:
    """True iff |supp f| * |supp fhat| == |G| (with f != 0)."""
    return len(support(group, f)) > 0 and uncertainty_product(group, f) == order(group)


def l1_norm(group: Group, f: Func) -> float:
    """The l^1 norm sum_x |f(x)|."""
    return sum(abs(f[x]) for x in elements(group))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subgroups, cosets, annihilators
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def subgroup_generated(group: Group, gens: Sequence[Elt]) -> List[Elt]:
    """The subgroup of G generated by the given elements (closure under +)."""
    zero: Elt = tuple(0 for _ in group)
    seen = {zero}
    frontier = [zero]
    while frontier:
        current = frontier.pop()
        for g in gens:
            nxt = add(group, current, g)
            if nxt not in seen:
                seen.add(nxt)
                frontier.append(nxt)
    return sorted(seen)


def all_subgroups(group: Group) -> List[Tuple[Elt, ...]]:
    """All subgroups of G, found by closing every subset of generators."""
    els = elements(group)
    found = set()
    # every subgroup of a finite abelian group of small rank is generated by
    # at most rank(G) elements; two generators suffice for the groups used here
    for r in range(0, 3):
        for gens in itertools.combinations(els, r):
            found.add(tuple(subgroup_generated(group, gens)))
    return sorted(found, key=lambda h: (len(h), h))


def annihilator(group: Group, H: Sequence[Elt]) -> List[Elt]:
    """H^perp = { k : chi_k(h) = 1 for all h in H }."""
    return [
        k
        for k in elements(group)
        if all(abs(pairing(group, k, h) - 1.0) < TOL for h in H)
    ]


def is_coset(group: Group, S: Sequence[Elt]) -> bool:
    """True iff the nonempty set S is a coset a + H of some subgroup H."""
    if not S:
        return False
    a = S[0]
    shifted = sorted(sub(group, s, a) for s in S)
    # a shifted copy is a subgroup iff it is closed under addition
    shifted_set = set(shifted)
    return all(add(group, u, v) in shifted_set for u in shifted for v in shifted)


def coset_modulation(
    group: Group, H: Sequence[Elt], a: Elt, chi: Elt, c: complex
) -> Func:
    """The modulated coset indicator f = c * chi_chi * 1_{a+H}."""
    Hset = set(H)
    return {
        x: (c * pairing(group, chi, x) if sub(group, x, a) in Hset else 0j)
        for x in elements(group)
    }


def indicator(group: Group, S: Iterable[Elt]) -> Func:
    """The 0/1 indicator function of a subset S of G."""
    Sset = set(S)
    return {x: (1.0 + 0j if x in Sset else 0j) for x in elements(group)}


def phase_subgroup(group: Group, f: Func) -> List[Elt]:
    """
    { z : chi_k(z) = chi_k0(z) for every k in supp fhat },
    where k0 is the first spectral frequency.  For an extremal f this is the
    period group of supp f.
    """
    spectrum = support(group, dft(group, f))
    k0 = spectrum[0]
    return [
        z
        for z in elements(group)
        if all(
            abs(pairing(group, k, z) - pairing(group, k0, z)) < TOL for k in spectrum
        )
    ]


def period_group(group: Group, S: Sequence[Elt]) -> List[Elt]:
    """{ z : S + z = S }, the group of periods of the set S."""
    Sset = set(S)
    return [z for z in elements(group) if {add(group, s, z) for s in Sset} == Sset]

    character: Elt
    scalar: complex
    modulus: float          # the constant value of |f| on the support
    spectrum: List[Elt]     # supp fhat, equal to character + subgroup^perp


def elements(group: Group) -> List[Elt]:
    return [tuple(t) for t in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in group))]


def add(group: Group, x: Elt, y: Elt) -> Elt:
    return tuple((a + b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def sub(group: Group, x: Elt, y: Elt) -> Elt:
    return tuple((a - b) % n for a, b, n in zip(x, y, group))


def pairing(group: Group, k: Elt, x: Elt) -> complex:
    return cmath.exp(
        2j * math.pi * sum(kj * xj / n for kj, xj, n in zip(k, x, group))
    )


def dft(group: Group, f: Func) -> Func:
    els = elements(group)
    return {k: sum(pairing(group, k, x).conjugate() * f[x] for x in els) for k in els}


def support(group: Group, f: Func) -> List[Elt]:
    return [x for x in elements(group) if abs(f[x]) > TOL]


def certify_extremal(group: Group, f: Func) -> Optional[ExtremalData]:
    """
    Return the classification data if f is extremal, and None otherwise.

    Cost: O(N^2) complex operations for the transform (O(N log N) with a fast
    transform), then O(N * |spectrum|) for the phase subgroup, then O(N) for
    the remaining data -- so O(N^2) overall, dominated by the transform.
    """
    N = math.prod(group)
    S = support(group, f)
    if not S:
        return None
    fhat = dft(group, f)
    A = support(group, fhat)
    if len(S) * len(A) != N:
        return None

    # phase subgroup: the shifts on which every spectral character agrees with
    # the reference character psi0 -- this is the hidden subgroup H
    psi0 = A[0]
    H = [
        z
        for z in elements(group)
        if all(
            abs(pairing(group, k, z) - pairing(group, psi0, z)) < TOL for k in A
        )
    ]
    a = S[0]
    c = pairing(group, psi0, a).conjugate() * f[a]
    return ExtremalData(
        subgroup=sorted(H),
        base_point=a,
        character=psi0,
        scalar=c,
        modulus=abs(f[a]),
        spectrum=sorted(A),
    )


def verify(group: Group, f: Func, data: ExtremalData) -> bool:
    """Independently check that f really equals c * chi * 1_{a+H}."""
    Hset = set(data.subgroup)
    for x in elements(group):
        expected = (
            data.scalar * pairing(group, data.character, x)
            if sub(group, x, data.base_point) in Hset
            else 0j
        )
        if abs(f[x] - expected) > 1e-8:
            return False
    return True


def demo() -> None:
    group: Group = (2, 6)
    els = elements(group)
    H = [(0, 0), (0, 2), (0, 4)]
    a, chi, c = (1, 1), (1, 3), 0.8 - 1.2j
    Hset = set(H)
    f: Func = {
        x: (c * pairing(group, chi, x) if sub(group, x, a) in Hset else 0j)
        for x in els
    }
    data = certify_extremal(group, f)
    assert data is not None and verify(group, f, data)
    print("extremal:            yes")
    print("recovered subgroup:  ", data.subgroup)
    print("base point:          ", data.base_point)
    print("character:           ", data.character)
    print(f"scalar:               {data.scalar:.4f}")
    print(f"constant modulus:     {data.modulus:.4f}")
    print("spectrum size:       ", len(data.spectrum))
    print("(the recovered character is unique only modulo the annihilator of H,\n so it may differ from the one used to build f while describing the same signal)")

    g: Func = dict(f)
    g[(0, 0)] = 1.0 + 0j        # break the coset structure by one sample
    print("perturbed signal extremal:", certify_extremal(group, g) is not None)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo()

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import itertools
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

TOL: float = 1e-8


@dataclass
class AuditReport:
    group_order: int
    subsets_checked: int
    extremal_subsets: List[Tuple[int, ...]]
    rigidity_violations: List[Tuple[int, ...]]
    gap_violations: List[Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], int]]
    min_excess_by_size: Dict[int, int]


def spectrum_size(N: int, S: Tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
    """Number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of the indicator of S."""
    return sum(
        1
        for k in range(N)
        if abs(sum(cmath.exp(-2j * math.pi * k * x / N) for x in S)) > TOL
    )


def is_coset(N: int, S: Tuple[int, ...]) -> bool:
    """True iff the nonempty set S is a coset of a subgroup of Z/N."""
    a = S[0]
    H = {(s - a) % N for s in S}
    return all((u + v) % N in H for u in H for v in H)


def audit(N: int) -> AuditReport:
    """
    Complete audit over all 2^N - 1 nonempty subsets.

    Cost: O(2^N * N^2) with the naive transform; the transform of an indicator
    is a character sum, so each subset costs O(N * |S|).
    """
    extremal: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    rig: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    gap: List[Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], int]] = []
    min_excess: Dict[int, int] = {}
    total = 0
    for k in range(1, N + 1):
        for S in itertools.combinations(range(N), k):
            total += 1
            prod = k * spectrum_size(N, S)
            cos = is_coset(N, S)
            if (prod == N) != cos:
                rig.append(S)
            if prod == N:
                extremal.append(S)
            elif N % k == 0:
                if prod < N + k:
                    gap.append((S, prod))
                excess = prod - N
                min_excess[k] = min(min_excess.get(k, excess), excess)
    return AuditReport(N, total, extremal, rig, gap, min_excess)


def main() -> None:
    for N in (6, 8, 9):
        rep = audit(N)
        print(f"Z/{N}: {rep.subsets_checked} subsets, "
              f"{len(rep.extremal_subsets)} extremal, "
              f"{len(rep.rigidity_violations)} rigidity violations, "
              f"{len(rep.gap_violations)} gap violations")
        print(f"      minimal excess above N, by support size dividing N: "
              f"{dict(sorted(rep.min_excess_by_size.items()))}")
        assert not rep.rigidity_violations and not rep.gap_violations


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import itertools
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

Elt = Tuple[int, ...]
Group = Tuple[int, ...]

TOL: float = 1e-7


@dataclass
class BiflatReport:
    order_K: int
    order_G: int
    modulus_of_f: float
    modulus_of_transform: float
    support_sizes: Tuple[int, int]
    uncertainty_product: int
    bound: int
    closed_form_matches: bool


def elements(group: Group) -> List[Elt]:
    return [tuple(t) for t in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in group))]


def pairing(group: Group, k: Elt, x: Elt) -> complex:
    return cmath.exp(
        2j * math.pi * sum(kj * xj / n for kj, xj, n in zip(k, x, group))
    )


def analyse(K: Group) -> BiflatReport:
    """
    Build the evaluation pairing on G = K x K^ and verify bi-flatness.

    Cost: |G|^2 = |K|^4 complex operations for the naive transform; the closed
    form below reduces the verification itself to O(|G|).
    """
    G: Group = K + K                      # coordinates (x, psi)
    nK = math.prod(K)
    els_K = elements(K)
    els_G = elements(G)
    half = len(K)

    def split(p: Elt) -> Tuple[Elt, Elt]:
        return p[:half], p[half:]

    f: Dict[Elt, complex] = {}
    for p in els_G:
        x, psi = split(p)
        f[p] = pairing(K, psi, x)

    fhat: Dict[Elt, complex] = {}
    for chi in els_G:
        fhat[chi] = sum(pairing(G, chi, p).conjugate() * f[p] for p in els_G)

    mods_f = {round(abs(v), 6) for v in f.values()}
    mods_fhat = {round(abs(v), 6) for v in fhat.values()}

    # closed form: fhat(chi) = |K| * conj(chi(z, 0)) with z determined by the
    # restriction of chi to the second factor
    ok = True
    zero_K: Elt = tuple(0 for _ in K)
    for chi in els_G:
        cx, cpsi = split(chi)
        # chi(0, psi) = psi(z): the exponents cpsi are exactly the coordinates of z
        z = cpsi
        predicted = nK * pairing(G, chi, z + zero_K).conjugate()
        if abs(predicted - fhat[chi]) > 1e-6:
            ok = False
    supp_f = sum(1 for v in f.values() if abs(v) > TOL)
    supp_fhat = sum(1 for v in fhat.values() if abs(v) > TOL)
    return BiflatReport(
        order_K=nK,
        order_G=nK * nK,
        modulus_of_f=mods_f.pop() if len(mods_f) == 1 else float("nan"),
        modulus_of_transform=mods_fhat.pop() if len(mods_fhat) == 1 else float("nan"),
        support_sizes=(supp_f, supp_fhat),
        uncertainty_product=supp_f * supp_fhat,
        bound=nK * nK,
        closed_form_matches=ok,
    )


def main() -> None:
    for K in [(2,), (3,), (4,), (2, 2), (5,)]:
        r = analyse(K)
        print(
            f"K = {K}:  |G| = {r.order_G:>3};  |f| == {r.modulus_of_f:.3f} everywhere;  "
            f"|fhat| == {r.modulus_of_transform:.3f} = sqrt(|G|) everywhere;  "
            f"product = {r.uncertainty_product} = |G|^2  (bound {r.bound});  "
            f"closed form verified: {r.closed_form_matches}"
        )
        assert abs(r.modulus_of_f - 1.0) < 1e-6
        assert abs(r.modulus_of_transform - r.order_K) < 1e-6
        assert r.uncertainty_product == r.order_G ** 2
        assert r.closed_form_matches


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import math

from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

N: int = 12

def dft(f: List[complex]) -> List[complex]:
    n = len(f)
    return [
        sum(f[x] * cmath.exp(-2j * math.pi * k * x / n) for x in range(n))
        for k in range(n)
    ]


def supports(f: List[complex]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    s = sum(1 for v in f if abs(v) > TOL)
    a = sum(1 for v in dft(f) if abs(v) > TOL)
    return s, a


def coset_modulation(d: int, a: int, chi: int) -> List[complex]:
    """Indicator of the coset a + H, H the subgroup of order d, modulated by chi."""
    step = N // d
    f = [0j] * N
    for j in range(d):
        x = (a + j * step) % N
        f[x] = cmath.exp(2j * math.pi * chi * x / N)
    return f

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import math
from typing import List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

n: int = 5
TOL: float = 1e-8

Grid = List[List[complex]]


def dft2(f: Grid) -> Grid:
    return [
        [
            sum(
                f[x][y] * cmath.exp(-2j * math.pi * (k * x + l * y) / n)
                for x in range(n)
                for y in range(n)
            )
            for l in range(n)
        ]
        for k in range(n)
    ]


def counts(f: Grid) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    s = sum(1 for row in f for v in row if abs(v) > TOL)
    a = sum(1 for row in dft2(f) for v in row if abs(v) > TOL)
    return s, a


def picket() -> Grid:
    """Modulated indicator of the subgroup {0} x Z/n (a coset of order n)."""
    return [
        [cmath.exp(2j * math.pi * 2 * y / n) if x == 0 else 0j for y in range(n)]
        for x in range(n)
    ]


def chirp() -> Grid:
    """The evaluation pairing on K x K^ with K = Z/n."""
    return [[cmath.exp(2j * math.pi * x * y / n) for y in range(n)] for x in range(n)]


def show(ax, M: Grid, kind: str, title: str) -> None:
    if kind == "mod":
        data = [[abs(v) for v in row] for row in M]
        im = ax.imshow(data, cmap="viridis", vmin=0)
        plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046)
    else:
        data = [
            [(cmath.phase(v) if abs(v) > TOL else float("nan")) for v in row]
            for row in M
        ]
        im = ax.imshow(data, cmap="hsv", vmin=-math.pi, vmax=math.pi)
        plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xticks(range(n)); ax.set_yticks(range(n))


def main() -> None:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(11.5, 7.2))

    for row, (f, name) in enumerate([(picket(), "modulated coset indicator"),
                                     (chirp(), "evaluation pairing (chirp)")]):
        F = dft2(f)
        s, a = counts(f)
        show(axes[row][0], f, "mod", f"{name}\n$|f|$")
        show(axes[row][1], f, "phase", r"$\arg f$")
        show(axes[row][2], F, "mod", r"$|\hat f|$")
        axes[row][0].set_ylabel(

        "opposite ends of the uncertainty scale",
        fontsize=12,

import itertools
import math
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

def spectrum_size(S: Tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
    vals = [
        sum(cmath.exp(-2j * math.pi * k * x / N) for x in S) for k in range(N)
    ]

const TAU = 2*Math.PI;

function divisors(N){ const d=[]; for(let k=1;k<=N;k++) if(N%k===0) d.push(k); return d; }

function buildSignal(N, mode, hOrd, a, chi){

  const step = N/hOrd;
  const put = (x,re,im)=>{ f[((x%N)+N)%N] = [re,im]; };

  g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(cx-R,cy); g.lineTo(cx+R,cy); g.moveTo(cx,cy-R); g.lineTo(cx,cy+R); g.stroke();

  });
  g.fillStyle='#93a0b5'; g.font='12px system-ui';
  g.fillText('demodulated samples at the first spectral frequency', 10, 16);
}

  $('tMF').textContent=sp(modsF).toFixed(4);
  $('tMA').textContent=sp(modsA).toFixed(4);
  $('tD').textContent=(D/(scale||1)).toFixed(4);

  const v=$('verdict');
  if(prod===N){
    v.className='verdict ok';
    v.innerHTML='<b>Extremal.</b> The product equals N exactly. The support is a coset of a subgroup of '
      + 'order '+S.length+', the modulus is constant on it, and the demodulated samples have collapsed '
      + 'to a single point.';
  } else {
    v.className='verdict no';
    const excess = prod-N;
    v.innerHTML='<b>Not extremal.</b> Product '+prod+' = N + '+excess+

        ? ('. Since |supp f| = '+S.length+' divides N, the gap theorem guarantees an excess of at least '+S.length+'.')
        : ('. Here |supp f| = '+S.length+' does not divide N, so extremality was impossible from the start.'));
  }
}

['N','mode','H','a','c'].forEach(id=>{
  $(id).addEventListener('input', update);
  $(id).addEventListener('change', update);
});

*A guided tour of the rigidity theorem for the Donoho–Stark uncertainty principle on finite abelian groups.*

---

## 0. The one-sentence version

On a finite abelian group $G$ with $N = |G|$ elements, every nonzero signal $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ obeys

$$|\operatorname{supp} f| \cdot |\operatorname{supp}\widehat f| \;\ge\; N,$$

and **equality holds for exactly one family of signals**: the *modulated coset indicators*
$$f \;=\; c\,\chi\,\mathbf{1}_{a+H}, \qquad H \le G \text{ a subgroup},\ a \in G,\ \chi \in \widehat G,\ c \ne 0 .$$

Everything below unpacks that sentence, and then shows why the most natural guess about *how* to recognise these signals is wrong.

<details>
<summary><b>Prerequisites — click to expand: groups, characters, and the finite Fourier transform</b></summary>

A **finite abelian group** $G$ is a finite set with a commutative, invertible addition. The workhorse example is $\mathbb{Z}/N$, the integers modulo $N$; by the structure theorem every finite abelian group is a product of such cyclic pieces, so nothing is lost by picturing $\mathbb{Z}/N$ or $\mathbb{Z}/n \times \mathbb{Z}/n$.

A **character** is a map $\psi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\psi(x+y) = \psi(x)\psi(y)$ and $|\psi(x)| = 1$. On $\mathbb{Z}/N$ these are exactly the $N$ pure waves $x \mapsto e^{2\pi i k x / N}$. The characters form the **dual group** $\widehat G$, and [Pontryagin duality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontryagin_duality) gives $|\widehat G| = |G|$ together with a canonical isomorphism $G \cong \widehat{\widehat G}$.

The **Fourier transform** is
$$\widehat f(\psi) \;=\; \sum_{x \in G}\overline{\psi(x)}\,f(x),$$
with inversion $N f(x) = \sum_{\psi}\psi(x)\widehat f(\psi)$ and [Plancherel's identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plancherel_theorem) $\sum_{\psi}|\widehat f(\psi)|^2 = N\sum_x |f(x)|^2$.

For a subgroup $H \le G$, its **annihilator** is $H^{\perp} = \{\psi : \psi|_H \equiv 1\}$, and the single most important arithmetic fact in this whole story is
$$|H| \cdot |H^{\perp}| \;=\; N .$$

</details>

---

## 1. Play first, theorise later

Before any proof, get the phenomenon under your fingers. In the widget below, build a picket fence on $\mathbb{Z}/N$ — pick a subgroup order $|H|$ dividing $N$, a shift $a$, and a modulating frequency $\chi$ — and watch the uncertainty product sit *exactly* at $N$. Then choose one of the sabotage modes: delete one sample, move one sample, or re-scale one sample. Each sabotage is tiny. The product is not.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Three things to notice while you play:

1. **Divisors only.** Extremality is possible only when $|\operatorname{supp} f|$ divides $N$. Try $N = 12$ and a five-point support: the product can never reach $12$.
2. **The jump.** When $|\operatorname{supp} f|$ divides $N$ and you break the structure, the product does not creep above $N$; it leaps by at least $|\operatorname{supp} f|$. There is no near-extremal regime.
3. **The purple plane.** The bottom panel plots the *demodulated samples* $\overline{\psi_0(x)}f(x)$ for $x$ in the support. For an extremal signal they collapse to a single dot. That collapse — happening simultaneously for *every* frequency in the spectrum — is the true content of the theorem.

---

## 2. The two easy extremals, then the whole family

**A spike.** Let $f$ be nonzero at one point only. Then $|\operatorname{supp} f| = 1$, and since $\widehat f(\psi) = \overline{\psi(a)}f(a)$ never vanishes, $|\operatorname{supp}\widehat f| = N$. Product: $N$.

**A pure wave.** Let $f = c\,\chi$. Then $\operatorname{supp} f = G$ and, by orthogonality of characters, $\widehat f$ is supported at the single frequency $\chi$. Product: $N$.

**Everything in between.** Take a subgroup $H$, translate it to $a + H$, and put a character on it with constant amplitude. This is a *picket fence*, and its transform is again a picket fence:

> **Theorem (transform of a modulated coset indicator).** For $f = c\,\chi\,\mathbf{1}_{a+H}$ and any $\psi \in \widehat G$,
> $$\widehat f(\psi) \;=\; c\,\overline{(\psi-\chi)(a)}\cdot|H|\quad\text{if }\psi - \chi \in H^{\perp}, \qquad \widehat f(\psi) = 0 \quad\text{otherwise.}$$
> Hence $\operatorname{supp}\widehat f = \chi + H^{\perp}$, and the uncertainty product is $|H|\cdot|H^{\perp}| = N$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof</b></summary>

The transform intertwines the three elementary operations: scaling ($\widehat{cf} = c\widehat f$), modulation ($\widehat{\chi f}(\psi) = \widehat f(\psi - \chi)$), and translation ($\widehat{f(\cdot - a)}(\psi) = \overline{\psi(a)}\widehat f(\psi)$). So it suffices to transform the bare subgroup indicator:
$$\widehat{\mathbf{1}_H}(\psi) \;=\; \sum_{h \in H}\overline{\psi(h)} \;=\; \begin{cases}|H|, & \psi|_H \equiv 1,\\ 0, & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}$$
because $\psi|_H$ is a character of $H$, and a nontrivial character of a finite group sums to zero. Reassembling gives the stated formula, and the support is $\chi + H^\perp$ because the two other factors never vanish.

</details>

All of this is verified numerically in the companion computations at the end of this page, over every subgroup of $\mathbb{Z}/12$ at once, together with the sharp value distribution $|f(x)| = \|f\|_1 / |\operatorname{supp} f|$ that we prove in a moment.

---

## 3. Rigidity: four squeezes

Now the hard direction. Suppose $|\operatorname{supp} f|\cdot|\operatorname{supp}\widehat f| = N$. Write $S = \operatorname{supp} f$ and $A = \operatorname{supp}\widehat f$.

### Squeeze 1 — the spectrum is flat

> **Theorem.** If $f$ is extremal then $|\widehat f(\psi)| = \|f\|_1$ for every $\psi \in A$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof</b></summary>

Two inequalities produce the uncertainty principle itself. First, restricting Plancherel to the spectrum and bounding each coefficient by $|\widehat f(\psi)| \le \sum_{x \in S}|f(x)| = \|f\|_1$:
$$N\|f\|_2^2 = \sum_{\psi \in A}|\widehat f(\psi)|^2 \le |A|\cdot\|f\|_1^2 .$$
Second, Cauchy–Schwarz over the support:
$$\|f\|_1^2 \le |S|\cdot\|f\|_2^2 .$$
Chaining gives $N \le |S||A|$. If $f$ is extremal, the chain closes, so *both* inequalities are equalities. Equality in the first forces every term $|\widehat f(\psi)|^2$, $\psi\in A$, to equal its common upper bound $\|f\|_1^2$.

</details>

### Squeeze 2 — the phases align

> **Lemma (equality in the triangle inequality).** If $\bigl|\sum_j z_j\bigr| = \sum_j |z_j|$ and $T = \sum_j z_j$, then $|T|\,z_i = |z_i|\,T$ for every $i$: all summands point the same way.
>
> **Theorem.** Consequently, for extremal $f$, every $\psi \in A$ and every $x \in S$,
> $$\|f\|_1\cdot \overline{\psi(x)}f(x) \;=\; |f(x)| \cdot \widehat f(\psi).$$

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof of the lemma</b></summary>

If $T = 0$ then every $z_j = 0$. Otherwise put $w = \overline T / |T|$, so $|w| = 1$ and $wT = |T|$. Termwise, $\operatorname{Re}(w z_j) \le |z_j|$; summing gives $\operatorname{Re}(wT) = |T| = \sum_j |z_j|$, so the termwise inequalities are all equalities. A complex number whose real part equals its modulus *is* that nonnegative real, so $wz_i = |z_i|$; multiply by $T$.

</details>

### Squeeze 3 — the modulus is flat

> **Theorem.** For extremal $f$ and every $x \in S$: $\;|f(x)| \cdot N = \|f\|_1 \cdot |A|$, i.e. $|f(x)| = \|f\|_1/|S|$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof</b></summary>

Apply Fourier inversion, restricted to the spectrum: $N f(x) = \sum_{\psi \in A}\psi(x)\widehat f(\psi)$. Multiply by $|f(x)|$ and use Squeeze 2 on each term:
$$|f(x)|\,\psi(x)\widehat f(\psi) = \psi(x)\bigl(\|f\|_1\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)\bigr) = \|f\|_1 f(x),$$
*independent of $\psi$*. So $|f(x)|\,Nf(x) = |A|\,\|f\|_1 f(x)$; cancel $f(x)\neq0$.

</details>

### Squeeze 4 — a subgroup appears from nowhere

Combining Squeezes 2 and 3: for each spectral $\psi$, the demodulated value $\overline{\psi(x)}f(x)$ has constant modulus *and* constant phase across $x \in S$, hence is **literally constant**. Fix $\psi_0 \in A$ and define the **phase subgroup**
$$H \;=\; \bigl\{z \in G : \psi(z) = \psi_0(z)\ \text{for all }\psi \in A\bigr\}.$$

> **Theorem.** $S - S \subseteq H$ and $A - \psi_0 \subseteq H^{\perp}$; and then, for any $a \in S$,
> $$\operatorname{supp} f \;=\; a + H, \qquad \operatorname{supp}\widehat f \;=\; \psi_0 + H^{\perp}.$$

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the counting argument — the heart of the theorem</b></summary>

For $x, y \in S$ and $\psi \in A$, dividing the identity $\overline{\psi(x)}f(x) = \overline{\psi(y)}f(y)$ by the corresponding identity for $\psi_0$ gives $(\psi - \psi_0)(x-y) = 1$, i.e. $x - y \in H$. By the definition of $H$, every $\psi \in A$ satisfies $\psi - \psi_0 \in H^{\perp}$.

So $y \mapsto y - a$ injects $S$ into $H$, and $\psi \mapsto \psi - \psi_0$ injects $A$ into $H^{\perp}$:
$$|S| \le |H|, \qquad |A| \le |H^{\perp}| .$$
Multiply, and use extremality on the left and subgroup duality on the right:
$$N = |S|\cdot|A| \;\le\; |H|\cdot|H^{\perp}| \;=\; N .$$
The chain collapses, so both injections are bijections. That is the entire miracle: two soft inclusions become exact identifications the moment you notice their sizes must multiply to the same number.

</details>

Putting the four squeezes together with $c = \overline{\psi_0(a)}f(a)$ yields $f = c\,\psi_0\,\mathbf{1}_{a+H}$ — the **Rigidity Theorem**.

Here is the argument turned into a decision procedure: given a signal, certify extremality and, if it holds, *extract* the hidden subgroup, the base point, the character and the scalar.

{{algorithm:0}}

## 4. What rigidity buys

Once you know the extremals exactly, the consequences cascade.

- **Divisibility.** $|\operatorname{supp} f|$ divides $N$; and every coset really occurs, so the obstruction is exactly divisibility.
- **Prime dichotomy.** If $N$ is prime, an extremal is a scaled spike or a scaled character. Nothing in between.
- **Self-duality.** If $f$ is extremal on $G$, then $\widehat f$ is extremal on $\widehat G$; the coset $(a, H)$ maps to the coset $(\chi, H^{\perp})$.
- **Canonicity.** The phase subgroup does not depend on the choice of $\psi_0$: it is the group of periods $\{z : \operatorname{supp} f + z = \operatorname{supp} f\}$ of the support.
- **Orbit structure.** Two extremals with the same support differ by a scalar and a modulation. The extremal set is one orbit per coset.
- **A purely combinatorial corollary.** For a nonempty $S \subseteq G$: the indicator $\mathbf{1}_S$ is extremal **iff $S$ is a coset**.
- **A gap, not a slope.** If $|\operatorname{supp} f|$ divides $N$ and $f$ is not a picket fence, then
$$|\operatorname{supp} f|\cdot|\operatorname{supp}\widehat f| \;\ge\; N + |\operatorname{supp} f| .$$

The picture below places all of this in one plane: the hyperbola $|S|\,|A| = N$ with its forbidden region beneath, the extremal stars sitting on it above the divisors of $N$, and the orange gap segments showing the step that non-extremals must clear.

## 5. The trap: flat is not enough

Squeezes 1 and 3 gave us two memorable conditions:

- **(F1)** $|f|$ is constant on $\operatorname{supp} f$;
- **(F2)** $|\widehat f|$ is constant on $\operatorname{supp}\widehat f$.

Call a signal satisfying both **bi-flat**. Surely bi-flat means extremal?

Take any finite abelian $K$ with $|K| > 1$, form the *self-dual* group $G = K \times \widehat K$ of order $|K|^2$, and define the **evaluation pairing**
$$f(x,\psi) \;=\; \psi(x).$$
For $K = \mathbb{Z}/n$ this is the discrete **chirp** $f(x,y) = e^{2\pi i xy/n}$ — the finite cousin of $e^{ix\xi}$, and the waveform your car's radar sweeps out.

> **Theorem.** $|f| \equiv 1$ on all of $G$, and $|\widehat f| \equiv |K| = \sqrt{|G|}$ on all of $\widehat G$. Hence both flatness conditions hold in the strongest possible form, while
> $$|\operatorname{supp} f|\cdot|\operatorname{supp}\widehat f| \;=\; |G|^2,$$
> the **largest** value any function can attain. Bi-flatness does not imply extremality; it is compatible with maximal non-extremality.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the transform computation</b></summary>

Let $\chi \in \widehat G$. Restrict it to the second factor: $\chi_2 := \chi(0,\cdot)$ is a character of $\widehat K$, so by Pontryagin duality there is a unique $z \in K$ with $\chi_2(\psi) = \psi(z)$. A character of a product splits, $\chi(x,\psi) = \chi(x,0)\,\psi(z)$, hence
$$\widehat f(\chi) = \sum_{x \in K}\overline{\chi(x,0)}\sum_{\psi \in \widehat K}\psi(x)\overline{\psi(z)} = |K|\cdot\overline{\chi(z,0)}$$
by character orthogonality (the inner sum is $|K|$ if $x = z$ and $0$ otherwise). The surviving factor is unimodular.

</details>

### The moral

Squeezes 1 and 3 are *magnitude* statements, and magnitudes are cheap. Squeeze 2, in the form of the total-coherence corollary, is a statement about **phases coupled across the whole spectrum at once**: the demodulated function must be constant simultaneously for every $\psi \in A$. That simultaneity is what makes the phase subgroup an intersection with teeth. The chirp violates it maximally — every frequency individually sees a perfectly balanced signal, no two frequencies agree on the phase pattern, and the energy stays smeared over everything.

> **Flatness is a snapshot. Rigidity is a conspiracy.**

---

## 6. Where this shows up

- **[Compressive sensing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compressed_sensing).** The uncertainty principle is the obstruction to unique sparse recovery; rigidity identifies exactly which configurations are genuinely ambiguous — the cosets — and the prime dichotomy explains why prime-length transforms are so well behaved.
- **[Hidden subgroup problems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidden_subgroup_problem).** The phase subgroup construction *is* spectral extraction of a hidden subgroup, and the canonicity theorem says it recovers the true period group.
- **Coding theory.** Cosets are precisely translated linear codes, so "minimal Fourier sparsity $\iff$ coset" is a spectral characterisation of linearity.
- **Radar and spread spectrum.** Bi-flat waveforms — constant envelope, constant spectral magnitude — are exactly what engineers *want*, and the counterexample quantifies their price: perfect two-sided flatness is the antipode of concentration.

---

## 7. Open ends

**Stability.** If the product is at most $(1+\varepsilon)N$, is $f$ within $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})\|f\|_2$ of a picket fence? Squeezes 1–3 degrade continuously; the obstruction is Squeeze 4, whose counting step is stubbornly discrete.

**Exponent independence.** Combining Plancherel with Hölder gives an $\ell^4$ (additive-energy) form of the principle. Is its equality case the *same* family? Both proofs run on the same two mechanisms — a flatness step and an alignment step — which suggests the extremal family is independent of the exponent.

**A coherence defect.** Define $D(f) = \max_{\psi \in A}\max_{x,y \in S}\bigl|\overline{\psi(x)}f(x) - \overline{\psi(y)}f(y)\bigr|$. Rigidity says $D = 0$ for extremals and the chirp maximises it. A two-sided bound relating $D(f)$ to the uncertainty excess would fuse the two halves of this page — and would very likely settle the stability question.

---
